chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
One does not marry the Jewish woman, nor the Christian woman, upon (as an additional wife to) the Muslim woman.

key_terms.عَلَى: Upon / in addition to (indicating polygyny context)

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim man marry a Jewish or Christian woman if he is already married to a Muslim woman?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the condition of 'qarar' (residence) in the prohibition, indicating that a Muslim man may marry a Jewish or Christian woman provided she is not already married to a Muslim man, thereby resolving apparent contradictions in juristic opinions. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the specific status of the female spouse in the context of polygyny with Ahl al-Kitab. The ruling underscores the preservation of religious integrity within the household structure as understood in early hadith literature.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahy, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Do not marry the Jewish woman, nor the Christian woman upon (as additional wife) the Muslim woman’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A Jewish or a Christian woman cannot become a second wife, the first being a Muslim woman.’”
